clue.text: Bound volumes of the Bard's letters in the possession of Grub Street

indicators.note: what is in someone's possession is held inside their grasp, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: Grub Street was the London home of jobbing writers, so it stands for hacks

indicators.note: the letters of a name are just its spelling, free to be laid out in any order

parts.note: the word itself supplies the four letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's correspondence, bound up in volumes, ends up owned by the hacks of Grub Street.
explanation.walkthrough: Grub Street, a real London street, became shorthand for poorly paid hack writers.
explanation.definitionFit: Books with stiff covers are hardbacks, as opposed to paperbacks, so they are literally bound volumes.

clue.text: Engaged, like the girl Meriam in "Cold Comfort Farm"

definitions.meaning: first meaning: taken on for paid work

definitions.text: like the girl Meriam in "Cold Comfort Farm"
definitions.meaning: second meaning: in Stella Gibbons's novel Meriam is the farm's ... girl

explanation.walkthrough: Cold Comfort Farm is Stella Gibbons's comic novel of rural Sussex; Meriam, the hired girl, has a baby every year.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone engaged is taken into employment for wages, which is exactly Meriam's status at the Starkadders' farm.

clue.text: Note objection about £1 is raised again

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: a word placed about others goes round them, enclosing them

parts.note: an objection, as in no ifs or buts
read as one pound: I for one, L for pound

explanation.surface: A musical objection over a single pound coin being put back up.
explanation.walkthrough: £1 is read in speaking order, one pound, giving one then the L of pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A structure raised a second time has been constructed anew after being knocked down.

clue.text: Fall in, as Bill will on reaching maturity

definitions.meaning: first meaning: of a debt or lease, to reach the date for payment

definitions.text: as Bill will on reaching maturity
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a bill of exchange is payable once it matures

explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a boy growing up, but it is a bill of exchange, which must be paid on its maturity date.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt falls in when its payment date arrives, which is when a matured bill must be settled.

clue.text: The speaker's notes

parts.note: surface reading: the jottings an orator reads from
setter's reading: a loudspeaker, whose notes are recorded tunes played in public

explanation.walkthrough: The speaker is not a person giving a talk but a loudspeaker, and its notes are musical ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorded background tunes piped through loudspeakers in shops and lifts are the notes such a speaker emits.

clue.text: In Holmes's adventure the carbuncle was blue

indicators.note: the letters wanted are sitting in the words that follow

parts.note: running across the join of the two words, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: In the Sherlock Holmes story The Blue Carbuncle, the gem of the title is blue.
explanation.walkthrough: The story title makes 'blue' read as a colour; here it means unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue is a common idiom for being unhappy or low in spirits.

clue.text: Three-dimensional sleeping compartment abandoned by the French

indicators.note: something abandoned is left behind, so these letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: a cubicle is a small partitioned sleeping space
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A bunk in a three-dimensional sleeping compartment is left vacant by French travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubic describes a solid having length, breadth and depth, the three spatial measurements.

clue.text: Good companion sickening with a cold

parts.note: Companion of Honour, a British order awarded for good service
falling sick

explanation.surface: A trusty friend is coming down with a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British honour, so a deserving companion is a CH.
explanation.definitionFit: A chill is a mild feverish illness from being cold, much like a common cold.

clue.text: Cut down support rope

parts.note: to bob is to cut short, as with hair
a stay is a brace or prop

explanation.surface: Someone shortens a supporting rope.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship it is the line or chain holding the bowsprit down to the stem.

clue.text: Under firm governor, perhaps CERN have a point in sticking together

parts.note: the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters are only one possible version, free to be reworked

parts.note: His Excellency, the title of a colonial governor
taken as written
east, a compass point

explanation.surface: Physicists at CERN, under a firm director, find a reason to stick together.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, governor under firm puts its letters after the company; CERN is the Geneva particle physics laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: Coherence is the quality of holding or cleaving together, as particles do when they cohere.

clue.text: Crucial boundary brings victory in game

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a point of no return, after Caesar's crossing of the river
second meaning: in piquet, to win before the loser has reached a hundred points

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a card-game verb from piquet, where beating an opponent who has not reached the target score doubles the win.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar crossed this Italian river to start civil war, so it names a line which commits you once passed; the card term is a scoring verb.

clue.text: Sounds like one who won't jump at a long coat

indicators.note: the clue says outright that we want something said the same way

parts.note: a horse that jibs refuses to go forward at a fence

explanation.surface: A rider complains about a horse that refuses fences on seeing a long coat flap.
explanation.walkthrough: To jib is to balk, so a jibber is a horse that will not jump; in non-rhotic speech it matches the garment's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the long open cloth coat worn by Muslim men, also spelt jibbah or jubbah.

clue.text: Ides originally the first of March? It's a natural belief

indicators.note: asks for the word in a different, earlier form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word itself supplies four letters to rearrange

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the initial of the month

explanation.surface: A soothsayer's warning about the Ides of March, recast as an instinctive human belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Deism is belief in a creator known through reason and nature rather than revelation, the so-called natural religion.

clue.text: Short up and down platforms on the underground

definitions.text: Short up and down platforms on the underground

parts.words: Short up and down platforms on the underground
parts.note: surface reading: brief trips between the station platforms of the Tube
setter's reading: a moving staircase is a short run of travelling steps going up or down

explanation.walkthrough: The platforms are the moving steps themselves, each carried a short way up or down in a Tube station; the underground is the London Tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving staircase carries passengers between levels in stations, its steps acting as little travelling platforms.

clue.text: The athlete's path, littered with burnt-out cases?

definitions.text: The athlete's path, littered with burnt-out cases?

parts.note: surface reading: strewn with exhausted runners who have given their all
setter's reading: spent embers left after burning coal

explanation.walkthrough: A Burnt-Out Case is a Graham Greene novel and a phrase for someone exhausted; the setter means spent coals.
explanation.definitionFit: Old running tracks were surfaced with fine ash and coal residue, making a path for runners.

clue.text: One divides at Chiswick, for example

indicators.note: something dividing a word splits it in two by sitting in the middle

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone stands at Chiswick, in west London, splitting a group.
explanation.walkthrough: Chiswick Eyot is a small island in the Thames by Chiswick; 'divides' also fits an island splitting the river.
explanation.definitionFit: An ait or eyot is a small river island, and Chiswick Eyot is a well-known Thames example.

clue.text: Cubs made a mess lying in wait

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, an ambush; the definition reads as the act

indicators.note: making a mess of things jumbles them up

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Young scouts made a mess while hiding in wait to pounce.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambuscade is an old word for an ambush, the tactic of hiding to attack by surprise.

clue.text: Broadway's writer built round anonym

indicators.note: something built is put together from parts, so the letters are assembled into a new order

parts.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Broadway author constructs a story around a pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The American writer of Guys and Dolls stories chronicled the gamblers and hustlers of Broadway in New York.

clue.text: Trust me to smash the greatest possible amount!

indicators.note: smashing something breaks it into pieces to be put back differently

parts.note: seven letters for the fodder
the last two letters of the fodder

explanation.surface: A confident boast: rely on me to break things as thoroughly as can be.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun this means the utmost extent, as in doing one's very most.

clue.text: Mr Coward's acid drop
Retainer the cavalryman tried to spear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something that holds a guy rope in place
second meaning: in the sport of tent-pegging, mounted riders lance a stake from the ground

explanation.walkthrough: Retainer suggests a servant, but it is a thing that retains. Tent-pegging is a cavalry sport of lifting stakes at the gallop.
explanation.definitionFit: This stake holds down a tent, and lancing one at full gallop is a traditional cavalry skill.

clue.text: Quiller-Couch heard last words of actor's speech

indicators.note: what is heard is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: Sir Arthur Quiller-Couch wrote under the pen name Q

explanation.surface: The literary scholar Quiller-Couch listens to an actor's closing lines.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre the final words of one speech signal the next performer to begin.

clue.text: Cold travelling? It's something to do with the altitude

definitions.text: something to do with the altitude

parts.note: the tap abbreviation
a performer travelling is on tour

explanation.surface: A traveller with a cold remarks it must be the high altitude.
explanation.definitionFit: On a map, a contour line joins points of equal height above sea level.

clue.text: Running before the wind, this craft is beached

definitions.text: Running before the wind, this craft is beached

parts.words: Running before the wind, this craft is beached
parts.note: surface reading: a sailing boat driven ashore by a gale
setter's reading: a wheeled sailing vehicle made to race along the shore itself

explanation.walkthrough: Beached sounds like a mishap for a boat, but this one is meant to be on the beach, sailing on wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a wheeled land vehicle with a sail, raced across flat beaches by the wind.

clue.text: This will get things working — agreement is on the way

parts.note: an old word for yes
street, the abbreviation for a way

explanation.surface: A deal that gets a project going is now on its way.
explanation.walkthrough: Working is the brewer's sense of fermenting; in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Brewers add this fungus to make a liquor ferment, which is described as working.

clue.text: Like a magic character, one in a runabout

indicators.note: one item placed in another is held inside it

parts.note: split into run, kept whole, and about, the abbreviation c for circa
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wizard-like figure rides in a small runabout car.
explanation.walkthrough: Runabout looks like one word for a small car, but it splits into run and about, and c (circa) means about.
explanation.definitionFit: Runes were letters of old Germanic alphabets, often credited with mystical power and used in spells.

clue.text: Shakespearian heroine, not being a princess, makes some salad

indicators.note: what is not there is taken away from the word

parts.note: heroine of Troilus and Cressida
Princess Ida is the title of a Gilbert and Sullivan opera

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare heroine, being no royal, ends up fixing a salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Peppery salad leaves such as watercress or mustard and cress are eaten raw.

clue.text: Viper crippled on the road

parts.note: an asp is a small venomous snake
halt is an old word for lame

explanation.surface: An injured snake lies helpless on the highway.
explanation.walkthrough: Halt as an adjective meaning lame survives in the Biblical phrase the halt and the lame.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarry bitumen surfacing covers most roads, so the material stands for the road surface itself.

clue.text: Add to perfect letter

parts.note: taken as written
something perfect suits to a T

explanation.surface: An instruction to append something to an already flawless letter.
explanation.walkthrough: Tot up is the British phrase for adding a column of figures.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot, or tot up, is to total a set of numbers, summing them.

clue.text: Cut off at the end in a post office deal

parts.note: taken as written
the standard abbreviation
to deal with something is to cope

explanation.surface: A phone call cut short during a transaction at the post office.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar this term names the dropping of final sounds from a word, as in curtailed forms like 'th'.

clue.text: Disease affecting one's loaf, so traumatic at first

parts.note: Latin for therefore

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the initial of the word

explanation.surface: A diagnosis that something has troubled the brain, the slang loaf, traumatically.
explanation.walkthrough: Loaf is British slang for head, a red herring here: the bread is what the fungus spoils.
explanation.definitionFit: This fungal disease infects rye grain, so it can taint bread made from it.

clue.text: Rotate to negotiate bends

definitions.meaning: first meaning: share a duty in sequence

explanation.walkthrough: Rotate looks like spinning, but here it is staff rotating a duty, each doing it in order.
explanation.definitionFit: People alternate in a sequence, and drivers steer their vehicle around corners in the road.
